A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DrVoice research work. Their main text, equations, three figures, nine tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching material displaced by pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original DrVoice benchmark results, component and training ablations, computational-resource measurements, and data-scaling and forgetting analyses.

after.justification: v4 reports updated DrVoice benchmark results and an additional SRH-pretraining comparison, alongside the retained original experiments and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix C adds an alternative that trains SRH with a streaming-TTS objective while freezing the other modules. It also introduces DPO for speech-comprehension and instruction-following preferences, followed by GSPO on mathematical problems. These substantially extend the previously described training procedure, although the dual-resolution architecture and Core-Cocktail mechanism remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds training on ASR-derived speech-query preferences, Tulu-3 instruction-following preferences, and mathematical problems identified through the PRM800K link. This extends training data and supervision within the existing speech, instruction-following, and reasoning scope. The four headline evaluation benchmarks and existing appendix task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets in Tables 2 and 3 remain unchanged. Appendix C adds an internal training-method comparison: standalone Qwen2.5-0.5B T2M pretraining serves as the comparator for SRH-only streaming-TTS pretraining. Xiaomi/MiMo-Audio is added as a score source, without becoming a benchmark comparator.

E3.justification: The new pretraining comparison contrasts standalone T2M training with SRH-only training while freezing the encoder, adaptor, shared LLM, and text head. Table 2 also revises the stated BigBenchAudio baseline provenance from reproduced inference to cited scores, except reproduced MiniCPM-o 2.6; this does not establish reruns. Existing benchmark metrics and model sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a comparison of two SRH-pretraining policies, reporting UltraEval-Audio S2S scores of 47.66 and 56.66. The existing component, Core-Cocktail, grouping, scaling, and forgetting analyses are retained. The new RL paragraph describes training but supplies no separate RL ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. v4 introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces DrVoice's overall scores: OpenAudioBench 69.24 to 72.04, VoiceBench 76.02 to 80.17, UltraEval-Audio 47.66 to 56.66, and BigBenchAudio 66.3 to 74.0. VoiceBench SD-QA declines from 68.54 to 64.30. Table 3 changes ASR-WER from 11.2 to 8.36 while UTMOS remains 4.29. These are results for an expanded training procedure, rather than an unchanged-training comparison. Existing appendix table and figure values are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the Core-Cocktail interpolation equation are unchanged. The added projection dimensions explain the existing no-SRH ablation implementation; no new formal definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion strengthen the central empirical claim from SOTA on OpenAudioBench and BigBenchAudio with comparable performance elsewhere to SOTA on all four benchmarks, including VoiceBench and UltraEval-Audio. The architectural novelty claims remain unchanged. The nearly 50% GPU-hour reduction newly emphasized in the contributions was already reported in v3's analyses.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly attributes the streaming-pretraining gain to closer alignment between pretraining and downstream task formats. v4 removes the proposed remedy of feeding text directly into SRH from Section 4.2 and Appendix D. The remaining speech-text alignment gap and its architectural explanation are still acknowledged in Section 4.2; full-duplex and broader-modality limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 clarifies that the no-CSE ablation uses discrete speech tokens without Whisper features, and that the no-SRH ablation projects and splits hidden states for parallel prediction. Appendix C adds preference-data construction steps and two data-source links. Appendix A's existing hyperparameters, hardware, and timings remain unchanged, without RL-specific settings or budgets.

R1.justification: v4 adds Rafailov et al. (2023) for DPO, Zheng et al. (2025) for GSPO, and Xiaomi (2025) for MiMo-Audio as a BigBenchAudio score source. Section 2 and the broader positioning of dual-resolution speech modeling remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized revisions to the abstract, contributions, results discussion, and conclusion; expands two ablation explanations; adds two Appendix C paragraphs; and shortens Appendix D. It also updates the affiliation and author punctuation. The overall section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 add runner-up underlining and revised emphasis, Table 2 expands its caption, and Table 4 shortens its caption. Appendix Table 7 moves to page 18 and Table 9 to a separate final page. All three figures and nine tables are retained without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, v4 makes the ablation implementations and BigBenchAudio score provenance clearer and adds a quantified SRH-pretraining comparison. These provide a limited improvement in interpretability and documentation beyond the higher headline scores. The benefit is constrained by missing RL-specific settings and ablations and incomplete integration of the new training recipe with Appendix A. Removing the text-conditioned-SRH future-work proposal reduces discussion slightly, although the remaining alignment limitation is still acknowledged.
